result.notes:
174 rows: 44 for Results 3.4 (lines 48 to 51), 46 for Results 3.5 (lines 53 to 58), 84 for Table 1 (caption line 160, heading line 163, cells lines 164 to 183). A script checked that every quote is an exact substring of its line and occurs there once. Table 1 quotes are cell fragments and keep the Markdown backslashes of the text file (before the underscore of an accession and before a plus or minus sign); manuscript_value drops them. No quote holds an em dash.
Results 3.4: the GO terms named as enriched have 22 rows (the phrase on osmotic and oxidative stress has two; the MAPK cascade row names its second reading); manuscript_value equals the phrase column of named_terms_results_3_4.csv. R3.4-007, 018 and 030 are the statements that the clustered terms are the enriched ones. Six statements about clusters and frequency (R3.4-008, 009, 013, 024, 031, 035) are kind other because the draft gives no criterion.
Results 3.5: numbers, rankings from Figure 9, and for six quoted methylation differences a second row of kind inequality that tests the meaning the text attaches: R3.5-029, 031 and 033 (ploidy values under control conditions; their quote is the opening clause of the paragraph, so they point back in the text) and R3.5-041, 043 and 046 (interaction values). Set-level statements of the same kind: R3.4-017, R3.4-029, R3.5-026, R3.5-039, T1-003.
Table 1: T1-001 to T1-004 are the caption and the heading Chromosome (I-45). T1-005 to T1-084 are the cells, four per table row in the order gene ID, start, end, methylation difference; differences are read-pooled over all 22 libraries and end is start plus 2, as in the DML tables. The sequence accession has no row of its own: it is in the quote and item of each start row, and an expression that selects the pipeline row by set, sequence and start checks it (build_rows.py --with-accession adds one identifier row per table row if wanted).
Left out: section, figure and table numbers, citation years, digits inside gene names, the sentence on supplementary lists (I-27), statements about other studies or about gene function, the Gene Name and Category columns (Category is hand-assigned; I-24 for the CAD row), and sentences that only interpret.
Kind statistic is used for methylation differences, which are percentage points although the text prints a percent sign.
Pointers for the mapping step: a candidate expression for every row except R3.5-034 (a condition of the experiment) ran without error in eval_expressions.R, 229 expressions in all. Results and expressions are in /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-WGBS-gigas-ploidy-desiccation/ed665b6a-3457-5aca-a521-7838dbc31cfa/scratchpad/wf/mv-extract-results34_35/pointer_table.tsv; the rows are built by build_rows.py in the same directory. They reproduce all 80 cells and every number of the text within 0.5 except 68% (134 of 195 is 68.72). Two term rows are TRUE in the legacy test (R3.4-032, R3.4-037) and none at gene level.
Outside this task: point 3 of the header of 01_pipeline/09_go_enrichment_legacy.R still says that terms with p < 0.01 went to the semantic similarity plots, which I-48 contradicts.

IDS. The orphan section has IDs D3.5x-001 to D3.5x-010, as point 6 of the update for this run asks. The ID rule printed in the task text (D-orphan-001) predates that update; the two map number for number. NUMBERS. Nine printed numbers describe this study: 1,038 (line 62); 27, 24 and 2,351 (line 66); 200 and 61.5 (line 71); 200, 61.5 and 123 (line 115). The word single on line 109 is entered as 1. Every other row states a direction, a presence, a class or a design, has manuscript_numeric null, and needs an expression that returns TRUE or FALSE.

RULES APPLIED.
(1) One row per claim per sentence. A claim made again in a later sentence has its own row (the same genes on lines 84, 87, 96 and 102).
(2) Functional categories. Where a sentence presents a GO category as a result (lines 62, 63, 66, 67, 68, 69 and 111) the row is of kind inequality and asks whether the term is enriched. Reason: the literal reading (at least one gene with a DML carries the term) is true of every term named and separates nothing, and these sentences draw on Figures 6 and 7, whose legends call their terms significantly enriched (issue I-48). If the mapper prefers the literal reading, the expression is genes_significant > 0 on the same table and each of these rows returns TRUE. (1) GO category rows (kind inequality): the legacy expression asks whether the GO term that names the category, or the label of Figure 6 or 7 it corresponds to, has below_p_cutoff or top10 in the step 09 table of its set; the corrected expression asks for q_wallenius below config$go_fdr in the eligible universe of the corrected-mode step 10 table. All 21 such rows return FALSE in both. Each note says that the sentence holds if read literally (a gene with a DML carries the term), gives the gene-level count against its expectation, and names narrower terms that do pass the legacy cutoff (cell cycle 2, meiosis 3, homeostasis 1, metabolic process 24 of 775, DNA damage 3; each on one or two genes). (2) D4.2-003: the inventory allowed 'two or more terms under response to stress'; by name, 8 of 76 such terms are in the legacy heat list, so that reading would give TRUE for the legacy analysis. I tested the seven stress-response terms that the draft shows for heat (response to stress and six labels of Figure 7), none of which passes, so that one rule serves all category rows; the item and note say so. This is the row most open to another reading. (3) D4.2-004: the inventory's pointer was FALSE (711 of 2,351 heat DML, 30%, exceed 20 points in both ploidies). I read 'in both diploid and triploid oysters' as each ploidy showing the differences and return TRUE (68% of heat DML among diploids alone, 62% among triploids alone); the note gives the 30%. (4) D4.3-006 and D4.8-003 are TRUE for the legacy analysis (451 and 2,118 terms with p below 0.01) and FALSE at gene level; they are the two rows where the corrected result differs from the legacy one. (5) Gene rows use genes_with_dml_<set>_<mode>.csv, dml_gene_overlap_shared_<mode>.csv and gene_table_<mode>.csv.gz. Rows that name CAD with a category test the locus and flag I-24; rows that give the category alone (D4.3-008, D4.7-005) and the identity row (D4.3-014) also require a GO term whose name refers to apoptosis or cell death, tested over all GO terms of the gene and FALSE. (6) Meaning rows use diagnostic('table1_group_means.csv') where the locus is in Table 1 (CAD, nesprin-1, dihydropyrimidinase, LAP) and the read counts of united_cpg otherwise; thresholds use config$dml_difference. D4.3-016, D4.3-020, D4.9-008, D4.9-010 and D4.9-014 are TRUE as descriptions without a test, and their notes say which few libraries carry the pattern; D4.9-012, D4.3-005 and D3.5x-006 are FALSE. result.notes: Result: 177 rows (174 verified, 3 added): 127 match, 49 differ, 1 is not regenerated. B, quotes: every quote occurs verbatim on its stated line and is at most 250 characters; none was changed. D, expressions: the 225 expressions as given ran without error in eval_expressions.R from the repository root (it fails from any other directory), and every recorded value and status was reproduced; statuses follow the rule of step 13 and tolerances follow the rule in every row. The 228 final expressions (176 legacy, 52 corrected) were rerun from the final rows. C, semantics: each quantity was recomputed with separate code (Python on the CSV files) from the tables of steps 05, 07, 08, 09, 10 and 11 and from table1_group_means.csv and table1_library_values.csv: the Figure 5 values, the Figure 9 entries, distinct loci and classes, the 20 rows of Table 1 parsed from the manuscript (set, gene ID, name, accession, start, end, rounded value, order), rank, p and counts of the 23 named terms, their gene-level results in corrected mode, the cluster shares, ranks and similarities, the feature shares, the gene counts, the group and library values, and the identity of the shared set with the intersection of the two DML lists in both modes. An exact hypergeometric tail on the counts reproduces all 23 legacy p-values with line totals and the five p-values with transcript totals that the notes quote from I-43. All numbers in the notes agree with these recomputations, with one exception (R3.4-008, below). Mistakes found and corrected: (1) T1-002 was TRUE by construction, because it compared two tables that step 09 writes from one object; it now also requires the row counts of the draft's table. (2) R3.4-013 was FALSE only because step 11 cannot place two of the three terms; it now tests significance as well, which the pipeline can decide. (3) The note of R3.4-008 offered a keyword count of 40% as if robust; with a wider keyword list the share is 54%, so the note now says the verdict depends on the definition (the same check for R3.4-024 gives 14% to 16%, so that verdict is robust). (4) The items of R3.4-018 and R3.4-030 described a test of the labelled terms that the expressions do not make. (5) R3.4-005 and R3.4-006 cited I-45 in the item but not in the issue column. (6) The note of T1-005 was worded as if the ten top-ranked terms did not have p below 0.01. A, completeness: three statements were missing and are added as R3.5-047 to R3.5-049 (the nesprin-1 sites under control conditions; the baseline claim in the last sentence of line 56; the conclusion of line 58 that triploids do not mirror the diploid response). Not added, as in the first batch: the sentence on supplementary lists, the naming of the three ontologies, and the cells of Table 1 that hold accession, gene name and category (the accession is checked inside each start row, the DML set inside each gene ID row; the names agree with table_1_legacy.csv in all 20 rows). E: R3.5-034 cannot be regenerated; no pipeline table or setting holds the temperature. Points for a decision. (a) The rows that test a meaning use two criteria by design: for under control conditions, a difference beyond 20 points in the printed direction among the control libraries (R3.5-029 therefore matches although the printed -21 is not the control value of -26.9); for an interaction, equality of the printed value with the difference between the ploidies in the response to heat (all FALSE). A 20-point rule on the difference of differences would turn R3.5-041 and R3.5-043 to TRUE without any test. (b) The sensitivity analyses finished while I worked. In a one-off look, not used in any row and not reviewed: the control-only list of A4 holds 3 of the 10 ploidy loci of Table 1, the same three that pass the 20-point rule (F-box DNA helicase 1 among them, neurexin-1 and MADD not), and the tested interaction of A2 without overdispersion correction holds the nesprin-1 locus but not the CAD or the dihydropyrimidinase locus (99 of the 200 shared loci in all, none with the correction). A corrected expression taken from A2 would therefore return TRUE for R3.5-043 and FALSE for R3.5-041 and R3.5-046. (c) The positional expressions of Table 1 return NA, which step 13 reports as not comparable, if the regenerated table ever changes its set or accession in a row. The mapper's four findings were confirmed: the fourth LAP locus has 112 and 141 raw reads in zr3534_3 and zr3534_4 against cutoffs of 100 and 103 and is absent from united_cpg_corrected.csv.gz; the REVIGO distances are as stated; the withdrawn wording of what_it_counts is on lines 182 and 183 of 01_pipeline/09_go_enrichment_legacy.R; the transcript-total p-values recompute.
